title: El enano en tu puerta
desc: A giant woman, a big-headed boy and forty verses
setting: December, seven at night, a drum coming down your street, and doña Carmen has just elbowed you.

steps.speaker: Doña Carmen
steps.es: Ahí viene la Gigantona. Salí a verla.
steps.en: Here comes the Gigantona. Come out and see her.

options.en: Chocho, how big! Who is inside?
options.feedback: Reacted first and asked second, which is the right way round when something arrives at your door.

options.es: Ah, sí, ya la había visto.
options.en: Ah, yes, I had seen it before.
options.feedback: Perhaps. Saying so takes the moment away from the person showing you.
Fair on the first December. Doña Carmen just told you what it is.

steps.speaker: Enano
steps.es: Aquí está el Enano Cabezón, que viene de León...
steps.en: Here is the Big-Headed Dwarf, who comes from León...

options.feedback: Nothing to say. He is eight and he has forty of these by heart. Let him finish.

options.en: (Take out the phone to film it)
options.feedback: Everybody does. It also puts a screen between you and the one boy performing at your gate.

options.en: I do not understand a word.
options.feedback: Said in the middle of the recital, to the reciter's face.

steps.speaker: Doña Carmen
steps.es: Ya terminó. Ahora le toca a usted.
steps.en: He has finished. Now it is your turn.

options.en: Here you go, kid. That was good.
options.feedback: The coin and a word about the performance. He will remember the second part longer.
The coin goes across. He recited forty lines and got a transaction.

options.en: How much does one usually give?
options.feedback: Asking the price out loud in front of him.

steps.speaker: Enano
steps.es: Gracias, y hasta el otro año.
steps.en: Thank you, and until next year.

options.es: Hasta el otro año pues. Aquí lo espero.
options.en: Until next year then. I will be waiting here.
options.feedback: You have just told a boy he has a door to come back to. That is how the December round survives.
Small, and after all that it lands smaller than you mean it.
He is leaving anyway. Now it sounds like you were waiting for him to go.
